The D in D-Day merely stands for Day. 

This coded designation was used for the day of any important invasion or military operation. For military planners (and later historians), the days before and after a D-Day were indicated using plus and minus signs: D-4 meant four days before a D-Day, while D+7 meant seven days after a D-Day.

Herr svartstrupe (Saxicola rubicola hibernans) "står på pinne" for å gi fotografen et annerledes bilde; som et ekstra krydder har han dratt blinkhinna ned over øyet og satt seg skråstilt.

Å «stå på pinne» betyr å være svært tjenestevillig, nesten overdrevent klar til å gjøre hva som helst for noen. Uttrykket stammer fra falkejakt i Europa; falken satt lenket på en pinne og ventet, klar til å sendes ut når jegeren ga signal.

-----------------

Mr. Stonechat (Saxicola rubicola hibernans) "stands on a stick" to give the photographer a different look; as an added spice, he has pulled his eyelid down over his eye and is sitting at an angle.

"Standing on a stick" or "to wait on someone hand and foot" means being very helpful, almost excessively ready to do anything for someone. The expression comes from falconry in Europe; the falcon sat chained to a stick and waited, ready to be sent out when the hunter gave the signal.
